Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

international adjective

also international law, internationally, between nations, multinational, international relations

classical

Cic. Off. 3.69: aliud jūs gentium, aliud jūs cīvīle
Traupman 187: jūs gentium, international law
M-O s.v. international law

gēns, gentis f.

noun, third declension; its genitive plural gentium serves for “international”

a nation, a people; in the genitive plural, of the nations: international

Latin has no adjective for “international”; it puts the nations in the genitive: jūs gentium, international law, the law the Romans held common to all peoples.

Other words

  • inter populōs — between peoples

    phrase: inter with the accusative · also used · modern · M-O s.v. international relations: necessitūdinis ratiōnēs inter populōs (Egger)

    A description, not a word: international relations as relations between peoples.

  • internātiōnālis, internātiōnāle — international

    adjective, third declension · also used · modern · M-O s.v. international (Egger)

    A coinage from the modern languages, marked as such by Morgan–Owens, with multinātiōnālis and plūrinātiōnālis.

Examples

  • Itaque majōrēs aliud jūs gentium, aliud jūs cīvīle esse voluērunt

    So our ancestors held the law of nations to be one thing and the law of our own state anotherCic. Off. 3.69

See also national, foreign, world, law.

SourcesLewis & Short: gens · Lewis & Short: inter · Lewis & Short: populus

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: international; international law; international relations.
